passage:
Subject: Thank you, properly

Dear Mridul,

When my father was taken to hospital on Monday night, I sent you three lines and vanished for four days. You took the vendor call, redid my slides for the Thursday review, and told our manager I was "handling something" without asking a single question. I do not think I said how much that meant. I am back now, and I would like to take the Friday client visit off you, since you mentioned dreading the drive. Lunch is on me as well. And if you are ever in a crunch, tell me before it gets bad.

Gratefully,
Eshaan

qa.q: What did Mridul do for the Thursday review?
Why did Eshaan write instead of just thanking in passing?
qa.a: Eshaan felt indebted and thought the thanks had not been said properly.

qa.q: How does Eshaan plan to return the favour?
qa.a: By taking over the Friday client visit, paying for lunch and offering help before a crunch gets bad.

qa.q: How might Mridul have felt about covering without questions?
qa.a: Mridul was probably willing to help, and not asking any questions shows trust.

grounding: A colleague who was covered for during a family emergency thanks the colleague sincerely and offers to return the favour at the right time.

The call about Fatima's father came at 10 a.m. on the Thursday of quarter-end at the Toronto accounting office. She stood at her desk with her coat half on, staring at three unfinished reconciliations. Soo-ah took the folder out of her hands. "Go. I've got these. Text me the passwords from the car."
Her father's surgery went well. Fatima came back on Monday to find every file closed, with small sticky notes explaining each step.
She didn't just say thanks in the hallway. She wrote a card: "You gave me a whole day with my dad when I needed it most. I won't forget it."
In May, when Soo-ah's landlord gave her one week to move out, Fatima showed up on Saturday with her brother's van and packing tape, and stayed until the last box was up the stairs.

qa.q: What did Soo-ah leave on the finished files?
qa.a: Small sticky notes explaining each step.

qa.q: What was Fatima feeling when she wrote the card?
qa.a: She felt deeply grateful and indebted, because Soo-ah had given her a whole day with her father when she needed it most.

qa.q: How did Fatima return the favour?
qa.a: When Soo-ah had one week to move, Fatima came on Saturday with a van and packing tape and stayed until the last box was up.

qa.q: What might it have meant to Soo-ah to receive the card?
qa.a: Soo-ah likely felt valued and touched, seeing that quiet extra work was noticed and remembered 🤍

grounding: A colleague covers during a family emergency; the protagonist thanks her sincerely and returns the favour when it matters.

passage:
In the staffroom of the government girls' school in Nashik, Sarika found a neat stack of corrected Class 9 notebooks on her desk. For the four days her son had been in the children's ward, Pradeep sir had taken her maths periods on top of his own and marked every test.
She held the stack against her chest for a moment. Then she went to find him in the lab.
"Pradeep sir, you did my notebooks too? That was two nights of work."
He shrugged. "Your boy needed you. How is he?"
"Home and bored. Thank you. Really." Her eyes stung, and she didn't hide it.
Two weeks later the timetable showed Pradeep on board-exam invigilation the same morning as his daughter's school annual day. Sarika wrote her own name in the slot before he could ask.

qa.q: How many days had Sarika's son been in the children's ward?
What does Sarika holding the stack against her chest suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she feels moved and grateful, and a little overwhelmed by how much extra work Pradeep sir took on for her.

qa.q: How did Sarika return the kindness at the right time?
qa.a: She wrote her own name in the invigilation slot so Pradeep could attend his daughter's annual day.

qa.q: How might Pradeep see Sarika's thanks in the lab?
qa.a: He seems to feel it was simply the natural thing to do, and he is touched to see her sincere thanks and hear the boy is home.

grounding: A colleague covers the protagonist's work during a family emergency; she thanks him sincerely and returns the favour when he needs it.
